newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent stagnates at lower levels pre-NYMEX lull.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent stagnates at lower levels pre-NYMEX lull.

text.p: IPE Brent stagnated at earlier lower levels in midday trade on Thursday as the market awaited the open of NYMEX for fresh direction, brokers said.
June Brent was 11 cents lower at $19.40 a barrel at 1231 GMT, while gas oil was $1.0 cents higher at $171.75 a tonne.
"It's extremely quiet," one broker said. "We won't see much action until NYMEX comes in."
Traders said news Texaco had cut crude runs at the Nerefco refinery in Rotterdam had dented prices in earlier trade.
According to trader sources, Texaco had cut crude output by 10 percent overall in May.
That translated into a 20 percent cut for the second half of May, the source said

Despite the third day of losses, traders said the bullish signals left after Monday's 79 cent gains had not been wiped out yet. "It would have to settle much lower to wipe out Monday's activity," said another trader. "There's still room for a recovery.
Meanwhile, the eagerly awaited Brent June loading programme gave the market little to chew on, coming roughly in line with expectations -- with 38.4 cargoes in June against 41.8 cargoes in May.
Some traders had expected an even lower programme.
On the gas oil front, many traders said the market had a disappointing morning.
June gas oil was called to open $2.0 higher in line with NYMEX heat gains overnight and as it moved to play catch up with the May contract's expiry level at $171.75.
"It managed to get up to $172.75 earlier on but since then its drifted off," said one trader. "Nobody's pressuring it there's just a lack of interest."
